title: Isolation and Culture of Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cells from the Human Mandible
protocol: Select the appropriate donor who plans to undergo mandibular surgeries such as sagittal split ramus osteotomy or mandibular angle reduction plasty.
Prepare 30 mL of phosphate buffer saline with 1% penicillin and streptomycin in a sterile, enzyme-free centrifuge tube on the day before surgery.
Store the prepared preservation solution in a refrigerator at 4°C overnight.
Transfer the centrifuge tube containing the preservation solution to an icebox one hour before the surgery date.
Sterilize scissors, tweezers, and knives by autoclaving at 120 °C and 0.27 MPa pressure for 20 minutes on the day before surgery.
Prepare α-MEM culture medium by mixing minimum essential medium alpha (α-MEM) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin and streptomycin.
Mix α-MEM culture medium with 50 mM ascorbic acid, 10 mM β-glycerol phosphate, and 0.1 mM dexamethasone to prepare osteogenic differentiation medium.
Mix α-MEM culture medium with 1 mM dexamethasone, 0.2 mM indomethacin, 10 µg/mL of insulin, and 0.5 mM IBMX to prepare adipogenic differentiation medium A.
Mix α-MEM culture medium with 10 µg/mL of insulin to prepare adipogenic differentiation medium B.
Mix HG-DMEM with 100 nM of dexamethasone, 100 g/mL of sodium pyruvate, 25 mg/mL of vitamin C, 40 mg/mL of proline, 10 ng/mL of TGF-β3, and 1% of ITS to prepare chondrogenic differentiation medium.
Study three-dimensional computerized tomographic scan images and surgical simulation planning of the donors before surgery.
Select the mandibular site that the donor plans to remove in surgery and is rich in cancellous bone with bone marrow as the donor site.
Disinfect and drape the patient before operating.
Resect the selected donor site of the mandible using the ultrasonic osteotome blade.
Put the mandibular bone specimens into the preservation solution.
Place the preservation solution with bone specimens in an icebox until isolation of MSCs starts in the laboratory.
Get the bone specimens out of the preservation solution.
Dip the bone specimens in 1x PBS with 1% penicillin and streptomycin for 5 min on a clean bench of the laminar flow cabinet.
Clean the adherent soft tissue and blood blot on the bone surface using sterile wet gauze.
Fill a 6 cm sterile culture dish with 5 mL of α-MEM culture medium.
Put the bone into the sterile culture dish.
Cut the bone into small pieces (almost 2-3 mm³ volume) with a sterilized knife or scissor.
Hold bone specimens with tweezers.
Aspirate α-MEM culture medium from the culture dish using a 1 mL disposable sterile syringe.
Insert the syringe needle into the bone marrow cavity of the cancellous bone specimen pieces.
Flush bone marrow into the culture dish from all sides of the bone specimen pieces, repeating at least 5-10 times per side.
Repeat flushing steps until all bone specimen pieces turn pure white.
Remove and discard all bone specimen pieces with tweezers.
Remove other small fragments using a cell filter with 70 μm pore size.
Shake the culture dish softly to distribute flushed cells evenly.
Place the culture dish into a cell incubator for culturing at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2.
On the third day of culture, check cell morphology and growth status under a light microscope.
Remove half of the culture medium containing no adherent cells and tissue fragments.
Add 3 mL of fresh α-MEM culture medium.
At culture day 7, remove all the culture medium.
Add 5 mL of fresh α-MEM culture medium.
Refresh the α-MEM culture medium every 3 days thereafter.
Check cell morphology and growth daily.
Remove all the culture medium from P0 cells when they reach 70%-80% confluence.
Wash the culture dish gently twice with 1x PBS to clean residual culture medium.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin with 0.02% EDTA to the culture dish to digest the cells.
Shake the culture dish softly to ensure even distribution of trypsin.
Place the culture dish at 37 °C for 3 min.
Check the cells under a microscope; when 70%-80% of cells contract and round, add 2 mL of α-MEM culture medium to stop digestion.
Gently blow the dish surface several times with a pipette to dislodge cells.
Transfer cell suspension into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in α-MEM culture medium.
Seed P0 cells in culture flasks (25 cm) with a 1:2 splitting ratio to create P1 cells.
Repeat steps from 4.1-4.6 when P1 cells reach 70%-80% confluence for second-generation cells (P2).
Change the expansion splitting ratio to 1:3 after third generation cell passage.
Use P3 to P5 cells to conduct identification experiments.
Digest P3 to P5 MSCs using 0.25% trypsin with 0.02% EDTA, following steps from 4.1-4.5 for flow cytometric analysis.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1x PBS at a concentration of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer the cell suspension into microcentrifuge tubes with 100 μL per tube.
Add immunolabeled mouse monoclonal anti-human antibodies to the tubes.
Incubate the antibodies and PBS control at room temperature in the dark for 30 min.
Centrifuge the tubes at 800 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 0.5 mL of 1x PBS.
Repeat this step twice.
Load the tubes into the flow cytometer.
Count the fluorescence-labeled cell numbers using a flow cytometer with a minimum of 10,000 events.
If not immediately counted, fix the cells in 1% paraformaldehyde and store at 4 °C in the dark for up to 24 h.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with α-MEM culture medium.

Count the cell number with a hemocytometer, and seed the cells on 96-well culture plates at a density of 3 x 10^3 cells per well, a total of 35 wells, 5 wells for each counting day (at day 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7).
Refresh the culture medium of cells every 3 days.
Discard α-MEM culture medium of the certain five wells for the certain counting day.
Add 100 µL of culture medium and 10 µL of CCK-8 solution to each well on the counting day.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Place the culture plates in a microplate spectrophotometer and measure the optical density value of five wells for each counting day (a total of 7 counting days) at a wavelength of 450 nm.
Use five wells of the culture medium without cells as blanks.
Record the optical density value of every well.
Calculate the average value and standard deviation of five wells for each counting day.
Plot the cell growth curve based on the data obtained.
Digest P3 cells with trypsin following steps 4.1-4.5.
Seed the cells at 2 x 10^5 cells/cm^2 in a 6-well plate.
Add 2.5 mL of α-MEM culture medium per well.
Change the culture medium into osteogenic induction medium when the cells reach 60%-70% confluence.
Change the induction medium every 3 days.
Check the cells under a microscope every 3 days after induction.
Observe cell morphology and look for obvious mineralization nodes.
Wash the cells twice with 1x PBS gently after 7 days of induction.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde to fix the cells at room temperature for 30 min.
Wash the cells twice with 1x PBS.
Add ALP staining solution and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Wash the cells with water to stop the ALP staining reaction.
Observe blue pigmented granules in the cells under a light microscope.
Capture photos of the stained cells.
Use Image J software to quantitatively analyze the staining degree.
Perform alizarin red staining to evaluate mineralization capacity after 21 days of induction.
Wash cells twice gently using 1x PBS.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde to fix the cells at room temperature for 30 min.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS twice.
Add 0.1% alizarin red staining solution and incubate for 20 min.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS twice.
Observe the red nodules among fixed cells under a light microscope.
Capture photos of the observed red nodules.
Add 10% cetylpyridinium chloride to the alizarin red-stained cells and incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Aspirate 50 μL of the CPC solution.
Measure the optical density (OD) at a wavelength of 540 nm using a microplate spectrophotometer.
Seed P3 cells in a 6-well plate following step 7.1 procedures.
Change the culture medium into adipogenic differentiation medium A when cells reach 80%-90% confluence.
Incubate the cells with adipogenic differentiation medium A at 37 °C for 3 days.
Change the induction medium to adipogenic differentiation medium B and incubate for 1 day.
Change the medium back to adipogenic differentiation medium A and incubate for 3 days.
Replace with medium B for 1 day.
Repeat this cycle 3-5 times until lipid droplets can be seen under the microscope.
Culture cells for an additional 7 days using adipogenic differentiation medium B after induction.
Refresh the medium B every 3 days.
Remove the induction medium and wash the cells gently with 1x PBS.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde to fix the cells at room temperature for 10 min.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS twice.
Incubate the cells with oil red O staining solution (1 mL per well) for 15 min.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS twice.
Place the cells under a microscope and observe the red lipid droplets to evaluate adipogenesis of differentiated cells.
Digest and transfer P3 cells into a 15 mL centrifuge tube containing 5 x 10^5 cells.
Centrifuge the tube at 250 x g for 4 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant by decanting carefully.
Add 0.5 ml of chondrogenic differentiation medium into the tube to resuspend the cells.
Centrifuge the tube again at 150 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Repeat the previous step twice.
Loosen the centrifuge tube cap to facilitate air exchange.
Place the tube in an incubator and induce the cells with 0.5 ml of chondrogenic differentiation medium at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2.
Keep the centrifuge tube stable without removing or shaking it within 24 or 48 h, until cells start pelleting.
Flick the centrifuge tube bottom to suspend the cell pellet in the differentiation medium.
Renew the chondrogenic differentiation medium with a pipette every 3 days.
Avoid aspirating away the cell pellet.
Induce the cells at least for 21 days until the pellet accretes to a 2 mm diameter.
Wash the pellet with 1x PBS.
Fix the pellet with 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min.
Dehydrate and paraffin embed the pellet.
Section the pellet with a thickness of 3 μm using a microtome.
Put the sections on glass slides.
Stain the slides with Alcian blue solution for 1 h at 37 °C.
Wash the stained slides with water.
Place the slides under a light microscope and capture photos of the blue-stained acid mucopolysaccharide indicating cartilage tissues.
